e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which is the short form of 'do not'?
e2.spell.contractions.hint: The apostrophe replaces the missing letter.
e2.spell.contractions.explain: do not -> don't. The apostrophe takes the place of the missing o.

e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which is the short form of 'cannot'?
e2.spell.contractions.hint: Two letters go missing: n and o.
e2.spell.contractions.explain: cannot -> can't. The apostrophe replaces the missing 'no'.

e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which is the short form of 'I am'?
e2.spell.contractions.explain: I am -> I'm. The apostrophe replaces the missing a.

e2.spell.contractions.hint: The apostrophe shows a letter is missing.
e2.spell.contractions.explain: it's is short for it is. (its with no apostrophe means belonging to it.)

e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which is the short form of 'she will'?
Which is the short form of 'we are'?
Which is the short form of 'did not'?
e2.spell.contractions.hint: The apostrophe goes where the o was.

e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which sentence uses a contraction correctly?
e2.spell.contractions.explain: have not -> haven't, with the apostrophe where the o was.

e2.spell.contractions.hint: It is not the same as 'there' or 'their'!

e2.spell.contractions.prompt: Which is the short form of 'was not'?
e2.spell.contractions.hint: The apostrophe replaces the o in not.

e2.spell.dge-ge.hint: A short vowel sound before the j sound needs 'dge'.
e2.spell.dge-ge.explain: bridge uses 'dge' because the vowel before it is short.

e2.spell.dge-ge.hint: The 'a' says its name, so no d is needed.
e2.spell.dge-ge.explain: cage uses 'ge' because the vowel sound is long.
badge uses 'dge' after the short a.
huge uses 'ge' because the u sound is long.

e2.spell.dge-ge.hint: Short 'i' sound before the j sound.
e2.spell.dge-ge.explain: fridge uses 'dge' after the short i.

e2.spell.dge-ge.hint: There is an n before the j sound.
e2.spell.dge-ge.explain: change uses 'ge'. We never use 'dge' after n.
hedge uses 'dge' after the short e.
page uses 'ge' because the vowel sound is long.
judge uses 'dge' after the short u.

e2.spell.dge-ge.prompt: Which word uses 'g' on its own for the j sound?
e2.spell.dge-ge.hint: Listen for a j sound at the start.
e2.spell.dge-ge.explain: In giant the letter g makes a j sound because it is followed by i.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: There is a silent letter at the start.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: knee starts with a silent k.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: You do this with a pencil. It has a silent w.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: write starts with a silent w.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: A little garden statue, with a silent g.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: gnome starts with a silent g.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: What you do on a door. Silent k.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: knock starts with a silent k.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: The opposite of right. Silent w.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: wrong starts with a silent w.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: You cut with it. Silent k.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: knife starts with a silent k.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: It is part of your arm. Silent w.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: wrist starts with a silent w.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: What a mouse does to cheese. Silent g.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: gnaw starts with a silent g.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: This one means to understand something.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: know (to understand) starts with a silent k. 'no' is the opposite of yes.

e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.hint: What you do to a present. Silent w.
e2.spell.kn-gn-wr.explain: wrap (to cover something) starts with a silent w.

e2.spell.le-el-al-il.explain: table ends in -le, the most common spelling of this sound.
tunnel ends in -el. This spelling often follows m, n, r, s, v and w.

e2.spell.le-el-al-il.hint: This is one of the rare -il words.
e2.spell.le-el-al-il.explain: pencil ends in -il. Only a few words do: pencil, fossil, nostril, April.

e2.spell.le-el-al-il.hint: It comes after a v, so -el.
e2.spell.le-el-al-il.explain: travel ends in -el, which often follows a v.

e2.spell.le-el-al-il.hint: It comes after an m, so -el.
e2.spell.le-el-al-il.explain: camel ends in -el, which often follows an m.

e2.spell.y-sound.hint: The 'igh' sound at the end of a word is often just y.
e2.spell.y-sound.explain: cry ends in y, which makes the long i sound.
fly ends in y making the long i sound.

e2.spell.y-sound.hint: It is a month with a capital letter.
e2.spell.y-sound.explain: July ends in y making the long i sound.
reply ends in y making the long i sound.
dry ends in y making the long i sound.

e2.spell.y-sound.hint: It means a bit quiet around new people.
e2.spell.y-sound.explain: shy ends in y making the long i sound.

e2.spell.y-sound.prompt: In which word does y sound like 'ee'?
e2.spell.y-sound.hint: Say each word and listen to the very end.
e2.spell.y-sound.explain: In happy the y makes an 'ee' sound. In sky, why and try it makes a long i sound.

e2.spell.y-sound.hint: A maths word ending in the long i sound.
e2.spell.y-sound.explain: multiply ends in y making the long i sound.

e2.spell.suffixes.hint: Just add the letters on the end.
Keep the root word the same.

e2.spell.suffixes.explain: care + ful = careful. The suffix -ful always has one l.

e2.spell.suffixes.hint: The y changes to an i.
e2.spell.suffixes.explain: happy + ness = happiness. The y becomes an i before the suffix.

e2.spell.suffixes.hint: The y changes to an i.
e2.spell.suffixes.explain: beauty + ful = beautiful. The y becomes an i.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'I can ___ the birds singing.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: This one has 'ear' hidden in it.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: hear is what you do with your ears. here means this place.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'Come and sit over ___.'
e2.spell.homophones.explain: here means this place. hear is what you do with your ears.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: '___ are three cats.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: This one is about a place or about something existing.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: There are three cats. 'There' is used for place or to say something exists.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'The children put on ___ coats.'
Choose the right word: 'I ate the whole ___ of bread.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: A whole one of these is a lot of bread.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: A loaf of bread is a whole one, before it is sliced.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'The wind ___ the leaves away.'
e2.spell.homophones.explain: blew is the past of blow. blue is a colour.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'My favourite colour is ___.'
e2.spell.homophones.explain: blue is the colour. blew is the past of blow.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'I have ___ apples.'
e2.spell.homophones.explain: two is the number. to shows direction. too means 'as well' or 'very'.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'It is much ___ hot in here.'
e2.spell.homophones.explain: too means very much or as well.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'The dog wagged ___ tail.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: The tail belongs to the dog. No apostrophe needed.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: its shows belonging. it's is short for 'it is'.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'We ___ our new bikes.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: You do this with your eyes.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: see is with your eyes. sea is the salty water.

e2.spell.homophones.prompt: Choose the right word: 'I found a shell by the ___.'
e2.spell.homophones.hint: It is full of salty water.
e2.spell.homophones.explain: sea is the water. see is with your eyes.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: Which is correct? The bag belonging to Sam.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.hint: Add an apostrophe then an s to the owner's name.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.explain: Sam's bag. The apostrophe before the s shows the bag belongs to Sam.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: Which is correct? The tail belonging to the dog.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.explain: the dog's tail. One owner takes apostrophe + s.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: Which is correct? The hat belonging to my mum.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.hint: Put the apostrophe straight after the owner.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: What does the apostrophe show in 'the boy's book'?
choices: the book belongs to the boy
there is more than one boy
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.answer: the book belongs to the boy
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.explain: An apostrophe + s shows that something belongs to someone.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: Which is correct? The pencil belonging to Priya.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.hint: Apostrophe, then s, straight after the name.

choices: The cats' bowl is empty if there is one cat.
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.explain: The cat's bowl — the apostrophe shows the bowl belongs to the cat.

e2.spell.apostrophe-own.prompt: Which is correct? The car belonging to the teacher.
Which word in this sentence needs an apostrophe? 'The birds nest is high up.'
e2.spell.apostrophe-own.explain: The nest belongs to the bird, so it should be 'the bird's nest'.

e2.spell.tricky-words.hint: There is a silent h and a capital C.
These are the things you wear.
e2.spell.tricky-words.explain: clothes (things you wear) is spelt c-l-o-t-h-e-s.

e2.spell.tricky-words.hint: Big Elephants Can Always Understand Small Elephants.
It has 'rent' hidden in the middle.
This one means 60 minutes and has a silent h.
Two f's and an 'e' in the middle.

e2.gram.word-classes.prompt: Which word is a noun? 'The fluffy rabbit hopped quickly.'
e2.gram.word-classes.hint: A noun is a person, place or thing.
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: rabbit is a noun — it is a thing you can point to.

e2.gram.word-classes.prompt: Which word is a verb? 'The fluffy rabbit hopped quickly.'
e2.gram.word-classes.hint: A verb is a doing or being word.
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: hopped is the verb — it is the action.

e2.gram.word-classes.prompt: Which word is an adjective? 'The fluffy rabbit hopped quickly.'
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: fluffy describes the rabbit, so it is an adjective.

e2.gram.word-classes.prompt: Which word is an adverb? 'The fluffy rabbit hopped quickly.'
e2.gram.word-classes.hint: An adverb tells you how the verb was done. Many end in -ly.
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: quickly tells us how the rabbit hopped, so it is an adverb.
school is a place, so it is a noun.
enormous describes how big something is, so it is an adjective.

e2.gram.word-classes.hint: Which one is an action you can do?
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: swim is an action, so it is a verb.
carefully ends in -ly and tells you how something was done.

e2.gram.word-classes.prompt: In 'the tall tower', which word is the adjective?
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: tall describes the tower, so it is the adjective.

e2.gram.word-classes.hint: Look for a word telling you how.
e2.gram.word-classes.explain: beautifully tells us how she sang, so it is an adverb.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Which word fits? 'I wore my coat ___ it was cold.'
Which word fits? 'We line up ___ the bell rings.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.hint: It is about time — at what moment does it happen?
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: when tells you at what time something happens.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Which word fits? '___ it rains tomorrow, we will stay inside.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.hint: It might happen, or it might not.
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: if introduces a condition — something that may or may not happen.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Which word fits? 'I know ___ you can do it.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: that joins the idea to the verb 'know'.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Why did the plant die? Finish it: 'The plant died ___ nobody watered it.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: because explains why the plant died.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Which word fits? 'Wash your hands ___ you eat.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.hint: It tells you the order in time — which comes first?
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: before shows which thing happens first.

choices: I was happy because I won.
Because I was happy I won because.
I because was happy I won.
I was happy I won because.
e2.gram.conjunctions.answer: I was happy because I won.
e2.gram.conjunctions.hint: 'because' goes in front of the reason.
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: because comes just before the reason: because I won.

e2.gram.conjunctions.prompt: Which word fits? 'I brush my teeth ___ I get into bed.'
e2.gram.conjunctions.explain: before shows that brushing happens first.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Which sentence is in the past?
e2.gram.tense.explain: walked has -ed, so it already happened.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Change to the past: 'I play football.'
e2.gram.tense.explain: play becomes played in the past.
is reading tells us it is happening right now.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Which word is the past of 'run'?
e2.gram.tense.hint: This verb is irregular — it changes completely.
e2.gram.tense.explain: run becomes ran in the past, not 'runned'.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Which word is the past of 'go'?
e2.gram.tense.hint: It is a completely different word.
e2.gram.tense.explain: go becomes went in the past.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Which sentence has the tense mixed up?
choices: Yesterday I go to the zoo.
Yesterday I went to the zoo.
Today I go to the zoo.
Tomorrow I will go to the zoo.
e2.gram.tense.answer: Yesterday I go to the zoo.
e2.gram.tense.hint: Does the time word match the verb?
e2.gram.tense.explain: Yesterday is in the past, so it should be 'I went to the zoo'.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Which word is the past of 'eat'?
e2.gram.tense.explain: eat becomes ate in the past.

e2.gram.tense.prompt: Complete in the present: 'Every day she ___ her bike.'
e2.gram.tense.hint: 'Every day' means it happens now, again and again.
e2.gram.tense.explain: For something that happens regularly we use the present: she rides.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Which is an expanded noun phrase?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.hint: An expanded noun phrase adds describing words.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: the tall, dark tower adds two adjectives to describe the tower.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Add describing words to 'dog'. Which is the expanded noun phrase?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.hint: Look for adjectives before the noun.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: fluffy and brown describe the dog, expanding the noun phrase.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Which words are the adjectives in 'the cold, wet morning'?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: cold and wet both describe the morning.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Which is the best expanded noun phrase for a scary forest?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.hint: Pick the one with the most useful description.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: dark and twisted paint a scary picture of the forest.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: What is the noun in 'a bright yellow flower'?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.hint: The noun is the thing itself.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: flower is the noun. bright and yellow are adjectives describing it.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Which sentence contains an expanded noun phrase?
choices: I saw a huge, spotty ladybird.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.answer: I saw a huge, spotty ladybird.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: huge, spotty ladybird is an expanded noun phrase.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: What punctuation usually separates two adjectives in a noun phrase?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: A comma separates two adjectives: the cold, wet morning.

e2.gram.noun-phrases.prompt: Expand this: '___ castle stood on the hill.'  Which fits best?
e2.gram.noun-phrases.hint: Choose the option that describes the castle.
e2.gram.noun-phrases.explain: ancient and crumbling expand the noun phrase and paint a picture.

choices: I packed a hat, a book, a snack and a drink.
I packed a hat a book a snack and a drink.
I packed a hat, a book, a snack, and, a drink.
I packed, a hat, a book, a snack and a drink.
e2.punct.commas-lists.answer: I packed a hat, a book, a snack and a drink.
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: Commas go between the items, and 'and' comes before the last one.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: Commas separate the items in a list, and we use 'and' before the last item.

e2.punct.commas-lists.prompt: How many commas does this list need? 'I like apples pears plums and grapes'
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: You do not need a comma before 'and'.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: I like apples, pears, plums and grapes. That is two commas.

choices: We saw lions, tigers and bears.
We saw lions tigers and bears.
We saw, lions, tigers and bears.
We saw lions, tigers, and, bears.
e2.punct.commas-lists.answer: We saw lions, tigers and bears.
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: One comma between the first two items.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: A comma goes between lions and tigers, then 'and' before bears.

e2.punct.commas-lists.prompt: Where does the comma go? 'She is kind funny and clever.'
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: The comma separates the first two describing words.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: She is kind, funny and clever.

e2.punct.commas-lists.prompt: Which sentence does NOT need commas?
choices: I like cats dogs and rabbits.
I like red blue and green.
I packed socks shoes and a coat.
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: How many items are in each list?
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: With only two items joined by 'and' you do not need a comma.

choices: My favourite colours are red, gold and green.
My favourite colours are, red gold and green.
My favourite colours are red gold, and green.
My, favourite colours are red gold and green.
e2.punct.commas-lists.answer: My favourite colours are red, gold and green.
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: Commas go between list items only.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: The comma separates red and gold; 'and' joins the last item.

e2.punct.commas-lists.prompt: How many commas does this need? 'For breakfast I had toast eggs beans and juice'
e2.punct.commas-lists.hint: Count the gaps between items, but not before 'and'.
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: toast, eggs, beans and juice — three commas.

e2.punct.commas-lists.prompt: What is a comma used for in a list?
e2.punct.commas-lists.explain: Commas separate the items in a list so it is easy to read.

e2.punct.sentence-types.prompt: What kind of sentence is this? 'Close the door.'
e2.punct.sentence-types.hint: It tells someone to do something.
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: A command tells someone to do something. It often starts with a verb.

e2.punct.sentence-types.prompt: What kind of sentence is this? 'Where are my shoes?'
e2.punct.sentence-types.hint: It ends with a question mark.
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: A question asks something and ends with a question mark.

e2.punct.sentence-types.prompt: What kind of sentence is this? 'The sky is blue.'
e2.punct.sentence-types.hint: It just tells you a fact.
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: A statement tells you something and ends with a full stop.

e2.punct.sentence-types.prompt: What kind of sentence is this? 'What a beautiful day!'
e2.punct.sentence-types.hint: It starts with 'What' or 'How' and shows strong feeling.
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: An exclamation shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.

e2.punct.sentence-types.hint: Commands boss you about a bit.
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: Put on your coat tells someone what to do, so it is a command.
How tall you are! shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.

e2.punct.sentence-types.prompt: Which punctuation mark ends a command?
choices: a full stop or exclamation mark
e2.punct.sentence-types.answer: a full stop or exclamation mark
e2.punct.sentence-types.explain: Commands end with a full stop, or an exclamation mark if they are shouted.
Do you like reading? asks something, so it is a question.
